Example 6.6

Draw all possible samples of size 2 with replacement from a population consisting of units 1,2,5,6 and find the proportion of even numbers in the samples. Construct the sampling distribution of sample proportion \hat{p} and check that E(\hat{p})=p i.e. \hat{p} is an unbiased estimator of p.

Solution:

Given 1, 2, 5, 6 N = 4 n = 2

Population proportion p=\frac{X}{N}=\frac{2}{4}=0.5

Possible samples of size n = 2 in S.W.R. case are N^n=4^2=16 which are shown in the table.

The sampling distribution of sample proportions \hat{p}

$E(\hat{p})=\mu_{\hat{p}}=\Sigma\hat{p}f(\hat{p})=\frac{8}{16}=0.5=p.$

It means that \hat{p}=\frac{X}{n} is an unbiased estimator of population proportion p.

sections.title: 6.2.4 Efficiency — relative efficiency

paras.text: If there are two estimators, both possessing the property of unbiasedness which can be used for the estimation of a parameter, it is difficult for us to choose the best one between them. The efficiency property decides to prefer the one which has minimum variance. Hence efficiency is a selection criterion for efficient estimator between unbiasead estimators.

sections.theory:
6.2.4 Efficiency

If there are two estimators, both possessing the property of unbiasedness which can be used for the estimation of a parameter, it is difficult for us to choose the best one between them. The efficiency property decides to prefer the one which has minimum variance. Hence efficiency is a selection criterion for efficient estimator between unbiasead estimators.

Definition of efficient estimator:

If \hat{\theta}_1 and \hat{\theta}_2 are two unbiased estimators of the same parameter θ and Var(\hat{\theta}_1)<Var(\hat{\theta}_2), then \hat{\theta}_1 is efficient estimator than \hat{\theta}_2. Efficiency is generally expressed in relative terms as:

$R.E=\frac{\textit{Variance of efficient estimator}}{\textit{Variance of other estimator}}$

If 0\le R.E<1\Rightarrow\hat{\theta}_1 is efficient

If R.E>1\Rightarrow\hat{\theta}_2 is efficient.

که 0\le R.E<1\Rightarrow\hat{\theta}_1 موثر دی

که R.E>1\Rightarrow\hat{\theta}_2 موثر دی.

6.2.4 Efficiency

If there are two estimators, both possessing the property of unbiasedness which can be used for the estimation of a parameter, it is difficult for us to choose the best one between them. The efficiency property decides to prefer the one which has minimum variance. Hence efficiency is a selection criterion for efficient estimator between unbiasead estimators.

Definition of efficient estimator:

If \hat{\theta}_1 and \hat{\theta}_2 are two unbiased estimators of the same parameter θ and Var(\hat{\theta}_1)<Var(\hat{\theta}_2), then \hat{\theta}_1 is efficient estimator than \hat{\theta}_2. Efficiency is generally expressed in relative terms as:

$R.E=\frac{\textit{Variance of efficient estimator}}{\textit{Variance of other estimator}}$

If 0\le R.E<1\Rightarrow\hat{\theta}_1 is efficient

If R.E>1\Rightarrow\hat{\theta}_2 is efficient.
